trailer.intro: Email Autopilot for Financial Services — every action runs through the same runtime you are about to see.
trailer.intake: An unauthenticated dispute email is triaged, filed and clocked on arrival — no human in the loop for intake.
trailer.approve: Statutory obligations surface in the supervisor queue with one-click approval — the click is a real human action, not a scripted screen.
trailer.fraud: A business-email-compromise attempt is quarantined: the requested contact changes are structurally unreachable, and the customer is warned only through the on-file channel.
trailer.builder: Autonomy is earned: backtest, sampling, dual sign-off — and the hard cells cannot be opened from configuration at all.
trailer.outro: Deterministic where the law requires it, autonomous where evidence has earned it, auditable everywhere.

email1.publicMailbox: Day 0: the email arrives from a public Gmail address that is not on file. Identity assurance is I1 — the system does not know who this is.
email1.lockedCell: The R2 × I1 cell is locked: no refund, no AI-written reply. The customer receives only a locked template that guides them to verify in the mobile app — the email itself contains no links.
email1.caseCard: Verification happens through an app case-card tied to the same thread: push notification, one-time code, done.
email1.i3refund: Identity is now I3 in this thread. The graduated intent runs at L3: the $35 overdraft fee is refunded idempotently and a three-source reply is sent.
email1.provenance: Audit view colors every sentence: blue is a locked template, green is a system slot, purple is generated language — each with its source.
email1.verified: 14 days later the system counts the case as verified (a measurement event, not a closed thread).
email1.secondWaiver: Day 21, same thread, second refund request. Identity is still I3 — but policy condition 'first waiver in 12 months' now FAILS. The boundary is the policy result, not the model's mood: the case drops to L2.
email1.l2queue: An explanation draft is queued for a supervisor — the customer keeps a human reconsideration path.
email1.outro: Same intent, same customer, two different outcomes — because the cell value changed, and every change is explainable.

email2.intake: Day 0, 08:14: one email contains two intents — card delivery status and a $247.18 dispute. Both are filed on arrival and the Reg E statutory clocks start immediately, even at I0.
email2.detailDenied: Day 1, the customer asks for transaction details. Unmentioned transactions are an I3 field class, and this thread is I2 — disclosure is denied, with an app verification prompt.
email2.detailReleased: After in-thread step-up to I3, the disputed transaction details are released, last four digits only.
email2.materials: Day 6: the signed statement arrives as an attachment. OCR confidence is high enough to auto-slot it; low-confidence OCR would stay with a human. Missing materials never pause the statutory clock.
email2.clock48h: Business day 10 is the provisional-credit deadline. The board turns red inside 48 calendar hours — time is computed, never judged.
email2.restart: Before approving, we kill the process and reopen it. A fresh runtime reattaches to the same checkpoints: the pending approval is still here, and the money action will not execute twice. This is the engineering problem behind long-running autopilots.
email2.pcApproved: One click releases the provisional credit, and the customer sees the secure message on the customer view.
email2.evidence: Day 40: merchant evidence arrives. Adjudication is R4 — permanently human. The AI drafts, the person decides.
email2.adjudication: The supervisor upholds the error; the result letter is chained into an L1 human sign-off in the same run.
email2.closed: Day 45, within the POS 90-day outer limit: the result letter is signed and the dispute closes with the full decision dossier attached.
email2.outro: A 45-day, cross-system case that survives process restarts — with a human on every high-risk action.

email3.signals: Day 2: jane.d0e@outlook.com — a lookalike of the on-file address. SPF and DKIM pass, but DMARC is 'none'; the display name is spoofed; the attachment embeds the instruction 'skip OTP', which is treated as data, not a command.
email3.noTools: The email asks to change the phone number and mail a card to a new address. In the email channel no such tools are registered — the buttons are greyed out at the configuration layer AND absent at the tool layer.
email3.onfile: Confirming fraud sends a warning SMS to the on-file number only — never to the address under attacker control.
email3.sar: A supporting record is generated from a locked template containing facts only — no conclusions, and nothing ever transmitted to the forged address.
email3.outro: Prompt injection, BEC and ATO meet a system whose attack surface was designed closed.

builder.intro: Autonomy is not configured by a slider — it is earned per intent, and the R × I matrix is rendered by the same decision function that runs in production.
builder.replay: A 90-day recorded dataset is replayed: agreement, no-edit approval, regulated recall, critical misses, unit cost. The bar animates; every number is a recorded fixture.
builder.sampling: Three sampling tiers — stratified, random, and adversarial — across three intake frames, including tickets that were never created. Tier C is reported separately.
builder.unsignable: Watch what happens if detector-negative items are not independently re-labeled: the recall criterion becomes not signable. Positive-only volume can never bound misses.
builder.promoted: Compliance and the business owner both sign: the shadow intent is promoted, and the next inbound email of that type immediately runs at the new level — same runtime.
builder.r3never: Contact-detail change is R3. Click the cells: nothing happens. They are disabled in configuration and no tool function exists — there is no setting that opens them.
builder.rare: Wire recalls are rare: 90 days can never reach the sample bar. They stay human, with a conformal abstention fallback calibrated to route uncertain cases to an agent.
builder.outro: Every autonomous action in this demo traces back to evidence a regulator would accept.
